newsitem.title: KENYA: African states recognize new Zaire government.
newsitem.headline: African states recognize new Zaire government.

text.p: African states are lining up to recognise new Zaire ruler Laurent Kabila following the victory over the weekend of his Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation Congo-Zaire.
Messages of recognition broadcast on state radio in Uganda and Zambia coincided with similar statements by regional states Rwanda, Kenya, Burundi and Botswana.

Ugandan president Yoweri Museveni said he hoped the alliance victory would bring closer ties between the two countries, in a message on state-run Uganda radio on Monday monitored by the British Broadcasting Corporation.

"The tasks ahead of you and your country are enormous. Nevertheless I am confident and trust that you will live up to the challenges of rebuilding your country's shattered economy and give your people hope for the future," Museveni said.

"It is my desire and hope that, under your leadership, the bonds of friendship and good neighbourliness between our two countries will flourish to new heights. We pledge our support for you and your compatriots and look forward to working closely with your government for the benefits of our peoples."
Uganda publically declared its support for the rebels near the start of a seven-month campaign but consistently denied providing direct military assistance.
Rwanda's government, which also backed the rebels but denies supporting them militarily, saluted Kabila's victory.

"As the people of the Democratic Republic of Congo celebrate the political change that has occurred in their country, the Rwandese government and people would like to express support for this momenteous achievement," said a statement signed by President Pasteur Bizimungu.

Kabila declared himself president on Saturday as his forces entered Kinshasa, changing the country's name to the Democratic Republic of Congo. On Friday Zaire President Mobutu Sese Seko relinquished power and abandoned the capital.
Zambian President Frederick Chiluba sent a message of congratulations on Monday pledging to work with the new leader and recognize its right to self-determination.

"President Chiluba said Zambia recognizes and welcomes the new government and leadership of President Kabila. Mr Chiluba said Zambia pledges to work with the new government and respect all the international and bilateral treaties," said a message on state-run radio Zambia.
Zaire's new government was "acceptable" to Tanzania said General Robert Mboma, chief of the Tanzanian People's Defence Forces, according to state-run radio Tanzania.
The end of Mobutu's regime "has put an end to the long concern over the lack of security on the Tanzania-Zaire border," Mboma said.
Botswana also welcomed the changes in Zaire and recognised the new government.
"Botswana is happy that the changes have occurred with little loss of life or shedding of blood," the permanent secretary for foreign affairs, Ernest Mpofu, told reporters.
"We hope those who have taken over will take the country along a path towards an democratic order that is acceptable to the world."
